Rank order is EVIDENCE-LED: the mood edge is first because it is the only one with a pooled prevalence from a systematic review, the anxiety edge is second because it shares that anchor set and adds a class-level scoping review, and the ocular edge is third because all three of its anchors are therapeutic in framing and none is a natural-history cohort.

SPECTRUM GUARD, APPLIED TO ALL THREE EDGES, AND THIS IS THE BATCH'S MOST IMPORTANT IDENTITY FINDING: the catalog carries toxic-epidermal-necrolysis as a SEPARATE IDENTITY, but EVERY located anchor on this file merges Stevens-Johnson syndrome with toxic epidermal necrolysis or with SJS-TEN overlap. NO located anchor reports an outcome in this identity separated from toxic epidermal necrolysis, and the pooled 24.9 percent psychiatric prevalence cannot be split. This is the SECOND consecutive identity in this batch, after spermatocele in batch 86, where the catalog is FINER-GRAINED than the evidence, and it is recorded rather than resolved because the two are genuinely graded points on one clinical spectrum.

CONSTRUCT-SEPARATION GUARD, APPLIED TO THE ANXIETY EDGE: the located anchors name POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER as a distinct outcome alongside anxiety and the multicentre survey administered both a Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and a Primary Care Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder screen. A positive anxiety screen in a survivor of a near-fatal reaction may reflect a trauma response rather than an anxiety disorder, and the located anchors do not separate the two.

ACUTE-VERSUS-CHRONIC GUARD, APPLIED TO ALL THREE EDGES: the paediatric follow-up cohort located for the mood edge reports ocular involvement developing in follow-up in patients whose eye examination was NORMAL IN THE ACUTE PHASE. Any claim about a chronic sequela must wait for a chronic assessment and may not be inferred from the acute presentation.

NO MAGNITUDE IS STATED FOR THE OCULAR EDGE, because all three of its anchors are a management review, a therapeutic systematic review and a therapeutic pilot study and none reports a natural-history prevalence or severity distribution. The primary anchor also reports that keratoplasty and keratoprosthesis success REMAINS LOW in this population, so the edge may not be used to imply reliable surgical correction.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Psychological sequelae are the most consistently documented long-term outcome of this identity, and the located evidence supplies a pooled prevalence from a systematic review. A PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis registered with INPLASY, evaluating observational studies of psychiatric complications and quality of life in ADULTS WITH SJS AND TEN, included ten articles describing 1,123 CASES AND 2,687 CONTROLS, and found a POOLED PREVALENCE OF PSYCHIATRIC COMPLICATIONS OF 24.9 PERCENT across eight studies with fifteen study groups and 2,120 participants; the authors state that the overall quality of the studies was SUBOPTIMAL and the heterogeneity VERY HIGH at I-squared 96 PERCENT, and that survivors appear to suffer a high burden including POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER, DEPRESSION, ANXIETY AND QUALITY OF LIFE IMPAIRMENT (PMID 41174859). A survey at 11 US academic health centres of 121 ADULTS DIAGNOSED WITH SJS OR TEN by inpatient consultative dermatologists between 2009 and 2019, using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9, the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, a Primary Care Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder screen and the Short Form Health Survey, was conducted specifically to examine the chronic physical and psychological sequelae of which the authors note LESS IS KNOWN than for the acute phase (PMID 33950191). A multisystem follow-up of 16 PAEDIATRIC patients with SJS, TEN or SJS-TEN overlap at a median follow-up of 6.5 YEARS found HIGH CHILDREN'S DEPRESSION INVENTORY SCORES IN 2 PATIENTS, a small to moderate quality-of-life effect in 43 PERCENT, skin sequelae in 81 percent and new ocular involvement appearing in 2 patients whose eye examination had been NORMAL IN THE ACUTE PHASE (PMID 37494888). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that all three anchors merge this identity with toxic epidermal necrolysis, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THE MERGE IS THE FIRST AND LARGEST LIMITATION: the catalog carries toxic-epidermal-necrolysis as a SEPARATE IDENTITY, but every anchor on this edge enrols SJS TOGETHER WITH TEN OR WITH SJS-TEN OVERLAP, and the meta-analysis states its population as SJS AND TEN PATIENTS without a split, so NO LOCATED ANCHOR REPORTS A PSYCHIATRIC OUTCOME IN STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME SEPARATED FROM TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS, and the pooled 24.9 percent cannot be attributed to this identity specifically. That merge is clinically defensible, since the two are graded points on one spectrum, but the catalog resolves them differently and the mismatch is disclosed on the face of the edge. The pooled figure's own authors rate the underlying study quality SUBOPTIMAL and the heterogeneity at I-squared 96 PERCENT, so 24.9 percent is a very imprecise central estimate. The second anchor is a CROSS-SECTIONAL SURVEY of patients recruited at 11 academic centres and its instruments are SCREENING INSTRUMENTS rather than diagnostic interviews, so a positive screen is not a disorder diagnosis. The third anchor has SIXTEEN PATIENTS with a median follow-up of 6.5 years, of whom SEVEN had SJS, FIVE had TEN and FOUR had overlap, so its 2 high depression scores are small-numerated and its centre of gravity is the overlap and TEN groups rather than this identity. A finding is carried rather than smoothed: the paediatric cohort's authors state they found ocular involvement developing in follow-up in patients whose eye examination had been NORMAL IN THE ACUTE PHASE, and the same pattern of late-emerging sequelae applies to mood. Individual claims require a dated biopsy-supported or clinically definitive diagnosis with the SEVERITY GRADE, the BODY-SITE INVOLVEMENT PERCENTAGE and whether the presentation was classified as SJS, overlap or TEN documented, a diagnostic interview or validated diagnostic measure rather than a screening score alone, an explicit timeline establishing whether mood symptoms predate the reaction or follow it, and a clinical determination separating a depressive disorder from post-traumatic stress disorder, from adjustment to disfigurement and functional loss, from acute-care related distress and from bereavement.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a severe cutaneous reaction that leaves a persistent threat of recurrence: the index reaction involves near-total epidermal detachment and life-threatening systemic involvement, the patient is educated that the syndrome can recur on re-exposure to a drug, and the survivor is left with visible sequelae and ongoing symptoms, so a threat that cannot be discharged by any test produces sustained hypervigilance; that vigilance maintains a background arousal which presents as mood and anxiety symptoms, and the located finding that post-traumatic stress disorder sits alongside depression in the pooled outcome is what makes the trauma pathway the named vector rather than a purely reactive one.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at PRISMA-systematic-review-and-meta-analysis, multicentre-cross-sectional-survey and small-paediatric-multisystem-cohort class, following the file's existing dermatological, mucocutaneous and psychological pathway scope. The meta-analysis is the anchor that carries the edge because it is the only located source that pools a prevalence at all, 24.9 percent across ten articles, 1,123 cases and 2,687 controls, and because its authors' own statements that the study quality was SUBOPTIMAL and the heterogeneity I-squared 96 PERCENT are registered alongside the figure rather than after it, which is the only honest way to present a pooled estimate with that scatter (PMID 41174859). The multicentre survey is registered because its stated purpose is precisely the chronic psychological sequelae of which the authors note LESS IS KNOWN than for the acute phase, and because eleven academic centres is the widest sampling frame located for this identity (PMID 33950191). The paediatric cohort is registered for the LONG-TERM FINDING that matters most for this identity, sequelae emerging in follow-up in patients whose acute-phase examination was normal, including ocular involvement in two, which is the located basis for the requirement that any claim wait for a chronic rather than an acute assessment (PMID 37494888). Because all three anchors merge this identity with toxic epidermal necrolysis and none splits them, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and states the pooled figure as a merged-population figure.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: EVERY ANCHOR ON THIS EDGE MERGES THIS IDENTITY WITH TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS, WHICH THE CATALOG CARRIES AS A SEPARATE IDENTITY, and the meta-analysis states its population as SJS AND TEN PATIENTS WITHOUT A SPLIT: NO LOCATED ANCHOR REPORTS A PSYCHIATRIC OUTCOME IN STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME SEPARATED FROM TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS, so the pooled 24.9 PERCENT CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED TO THIS IDENTITY SPECIFICALLY and a TEN finding may not be transferred to this identity (PMID 41174859, PMID 33950191, PMID 37494888). THE POOLED FIGURE IS IMPRECISE BY ITS AUTHORS' OWN ACCOUNT: ten articles, 1,123 cases and 2,687 controls, but STUDY QUALITY DESCRIBED AS SUBOPTIMAL and HETEROGENEITY AT I-SQUARED 96 PERCENT across eight studies and fifteen study groups (PMID 41174859). THE SECOND ANCHOR USES SCREENING INSTRUMENTS rather than diagnostic interviews, so a positive PHQ-9, GAD-7 or post-traumatic stress screen is NOT A DISORDER DIAGNOSIS, and it is cross-sectional across 11 academic centres (PMID 33950191). THE THIRD ANCHOR HAS SIXTEEN PATIENTS at a median follow-up of 6.5 years, of whom only SEVEN had SJS against five TEN and four overlap, so its two high depression scores are SMALL-NUMERATED and its centre of gravity is the overlap and TEN groups (PMID 37494888). A LATE-EMERGING-SEQUELAE FINDING IS CARRIED: the paediatric cohort reports ocular involvement developing in follow-up in patients whose eye examination was NORMAL IN THE ACUTE PHASE, which is the located basis for requiring a chronic rather than an acute assessment before any psychological claim, and the same caution applies to mood (PMID 37494888). NO located anchor reports a depression DIAGNOSIS rate, a longitudinal course, a severity grade breakdown, or any effect of treatment or of long-term follow-up on psychological outcome, and the only anchor with an explicitly adult population is the survey, which is also the only one with a large sample.

sourceReferences.note: PRISMA SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS, REGISTERED WITH INPLASY, of observational studies of psychiatric complications and quality of life in ADULTS WITH SJS AND TEN, with potential bias assessed using the NIH criteria. TEN ARTICLES DESCRIBING 1,123 CASES AND 2,687 CONTROLS were included. THE AUTHORS STATE THE OVERALL QUALITY OF THE STUDIES WAS SUBOPTIMAL AND THE LEVEL OF HETEROGENEITY VERY HIGH AT I-SQUARED 96 PERCENT. Meta-analysis of eight studies with fifteen study groups, n EQUALS 2,120, showed A POOLED PREVALENCE OF PSYCHIATRIC COMPLICATIONS OF 24.9 PERCENT IN SJS AND TEN PATIENTS. The authors report that survivors suffer a high burden of psychological complications including POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER, DEPRESSION, ANXIETY and quality of life impairment, that the population would likely benefit from early multidisciplinary input and long-term follow-up, and that additional larger controlled studies are needed. Registered as the only located pooled prevalence, with the authors' own quality and heterogeneity statements carried on the face of the edge. DISCLOSED: the population is SJS AND TEN MERGED, and the pooled figure cannot be split to this identity.

THE MOST COMMON SEQUELAE WERE SKIN CHANGES IN 13 PATIENTS, 81 PERCENT, with hyperpigmentation in 9, 56 PERCENT. A SMALL TO MODERATE EFFECT ON QUALITY OF LIFE was found in 43 PERCENT, and 4 patients had height or weight percentile loss. IN TWO CASES THE EYE EXAMINATION WAS NORMAL IN THE ACUTE PHASE WHILE OCULAR INVOLVEMENT WAS PRESENT IN THE CHRONIC PERIOD. Three patients' anxiety screens and 2 patients' depression inventories were high, and 3 patients' antinuclear antibody values were positive at follow-up having been negative at first admission. DISCLOSED: SIXTEEN PATIENTS, of whom only SEVEN had SJS, so the two high depression scores are small-numerated and the cohort's centre of gravity is the overlap and TEN groups.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: This edge shares its first two anchors with the depressive-disorder edge and adds a third from a wider scoping review, and the sharing is the located finding: the psychological literature on this identity is small and measures anxiety and post-traumatic stress alongside depression in the same participants. The PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis of psychiatric complications and quality of life in ADULTS WITH SJS AND TEN pooled ten articles describing 1,123 cases and 2,687 controls and found A POOLED PREVALENCE OF PSYCHIATRIC COMPLICATIONS OF 24.9 PERCENT, with the authors naming POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER, DEPRESSION AND ANXIETY among the burden (PMID 41174859). The 121-adult multicentre survey at 11 US academic centres, whose stated purpose was the chronic sequelae of which less is known than for the acute phase, administered the GENERALIZED ANXIETY DISORDER-7 alongside a Primary Care Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder screen and the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PMID 33950191). A SCOPING REVIEW of MENTAL HEALTH AND PSYCHOSOCIAL OUTCOMES IN SURVIVORS OF SEVERE CUTANEOUS ADVERSE REACTIONS extends the evidence base beyond this one identity to the whole drug-reaction class, which is the located reason it is registered as a third anchor and simultaneously the reason its findings may not be attributed to this identity alone (PMID 40354513). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that the third anchor's population is a class and not an identity, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and THREE SEPARATE LIMITATIONS ARE STATED RATHER THAN RESOLVED. First, the MERGE: all three anchors concern Stevens-Johnson syndrome either merged with toxic epidermal necrolysis or generalised to a drug-reaction class, and the catalog carries toxic-epidermal-necrolysis separately, so no located anchor reports an anxiety outcome in this identity separated from TEN. Second, the CLASS POPULATION: the third anchor is a SCOPING REVIEW of survivors of severe cutaneous adverse reactions as a whole, which includes but is not limited to this identity, so it can supply breadth and cannot supply a rate for this identity; it is registered for coverage and that limitation is on the face of the edge. Third, the ANXIETY CONSTRUCT ITSELF: the strongest located anchor names post-traumatic stress disorder as a distinct outcome alongside anxiety, and a post-traumatic stress screen is a different instrument with a different threshold from the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7, so a claim that imports an anxiety figure from a mixed post-traumatic-stress-and-anxiety pool would misstate what was measured. The pooled 24.9 percent is a figure for PSYCHIATRIC COMPLICATIONS AS A WHOLE, not for anxiety, and the second anchor is a cross-sectional survey using screening instruments rather than diagnostic interviews. A point of emphasis is carried: for this identity, an anxiety screen that is positive may reflect a trauma response to a near-fatal reaction rather than an anxiety disorder in the psychiatric sense, and the located anchors do not separate the two. Individual claims require a dated biopsy-supported or clinically definitive diagnosis with the severity grade, the body-site involvement percentage and the SJS, overlap or TEN classification documented, a diagnostic interview or validated anxiety-specific measure rather than a trauma screen alone, an explicit timeline establishing whether anxiety predates the reaction or follows it, and a clinical determination separating an anxiety disorder from post-traumatic stress disorder, from illness anxiety about recurrence, from adjustment to disfigurement and from a pre-existing anxiety disorder.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is a trauma pathway with an added vigilance component: the index reaction is a near-total epidermal detachment with systemic involvement and a genuine risk of death, and the located evidence names post-traumatic stress disorder explicitly in the same pooled outcome as anxiety, so the named vector is the intrusive recollection, avoidance and hyperarousal that follows an event of that magnitude, compounded by a persistent and untestable fear of recurrence on drug re-exposure, which keeps the arousal active between appointments; the two components are named separately because the located instruments separate them, and because merging them would overstate what a Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 score measures in a survivor of this reaction.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at PRISMA-systematic-review-and-meta-analysis, multicentre-cross-sectional-survey and scoping-review class, following the file's existing dermatological, mucocutaneous and psychological pathway scope. The meta-analysis is the anchor that carries the edge, being the only located source that pools a prevalence, 24.9 percent across 1,123 cases and 2,687 controls, and its authors' own statements that the study quality was SUBOPTIMAL and the heterogeneity I-squared 96 PERCENT are carried alongside the figure (PMID 41174859). The multicentre survey is registered as the widest adult sampling frame located, eleven academic centres, and as the source whose explicit purpose was the chronic phase (PMID 33950191). The scoping review is registered for the reason that it widens the frame beyond one identity, so that a reader can see the shape of the psychological burden across severe cutaneous adverse reactions rather than inferring the whole of it from a small SJS-specific literature, and its class-level limitation is disclosed on the edge (PMID 40354513). Because the two identity-specific anchors merge with toxic epidermal necrolysis, because the third is class-level, and because the pooled figure is for psychiatric complications as a whole rather than for anxiety, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only and ranks it below the depressive-disorder edge, whose anchors are marginally better aligned to their target.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: EVERY ANCHOR EITHER MERGES THIS IDENTITY WITH TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS, WHICH THE CATALOG CARRIES SEPARATELY, or generalises beyond it, so NO located anchor reports an anxiety outcome in this identity separated from toxic epidermal necrolysis and a TEN finding may not be transferred to this identity (PMID 41174859, PMID 33950191). THE THIRD ANCHOR'S POPULATION IS A CLASS, NOT AN IDENTITY: it is a SCOPING REVIEW of mental health and psychosocial outcomes in survivors of SEVERE CUTANEOUS ADVERSE REACTIONS as a whole, which includes but is not limited to this identity, so it can supply coverage but CANNOT SUPPLY A RATE FOR THIS IDENTITY (PMID 40354513). THE POOLED 24.9 PERCENT IS A FIGURE FOR PSYCHIATRIC COMPLICATIONS AS A WHOLE, NOT FOR ANXIETY, and it rests on ten articles with STUDY QUALITY DESCRIBED AS SUBOPTIMAL and I-SQUARED 96 PERCENT heterogeneity (PMID 41174859). THE ANXIETY AND TRAUMA CONSTRUCTS ARE DISTINCT IN THE LOCATED ANCHORS: the meta-analysis names POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER alongside anxiety as separate outcomes and the survey administered both a Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 and a Primary Care Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder screen, so importing an anxiety figure from a mixed pool would misstate what was measured (PMID 41174859, PMID 33950191). A POSITIVE ANXIETY SCREEN IN A SURVIVOR OF THIS REACTION MAY REFLECT A TRAUMA RESPONSE to a near-fatal event rather than an anxiety disorder in the psychiatric sense, and no located anchor separates the two. NO located anchor reports an anxiety DISORDER diagnosis rate, a longitudinal course, a severity-grade breakdown, or any effect of treatment or of structured long-term follow-up on psychological outcome, and no anchor stratifies by whether the reaction was drug-induced, infection-triggered or of another trigger.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Chronic ocular surface disease is the most durable physical sequela of this identity, and the located evidence documents the rehabilitation problem it creates. A review of OCULAR INVOLVEMENT IN STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME AND TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS describes how the classification of ocular disease in the acute and chronic stages has evolved and how management has correspondingly changed; it states that to manage the CHRONIC STAGE it is of the utmost importance to CORRECTLY IDENTIFY THE UNDERLYING PROBLEM, and that alongside minor salivary gland transplantation and PUNCTAL OCCLUSION the REHABILITATIVE MANAGEMENT OF THE OCULAR SURFACE encompasses the use of specially designed scleral lenses, specifically Prosthetic Replacement of the Ocular Surface Ecosystem (PMID 41288622). The same review records that although the success rate of keratoplasty and keratoprosthesis REMAINS LOW, establishing good ocular surface homeostasis beforehand significantly improves the outcome, and that autologous mucosal membrane grafting has recently seen a resurgence (PMID 41288622). A systematic review of AMNIOTIC MEMBRANE TRANSPLANTATION in acute and chronic Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis addresses the chronic phase directly, and a pilot study of 5-Fluorouracil AS A TARGETED LACRIMAL GLAND THERAPY FOR CHRONIC STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME exists precisely because the lacrimal gland is the structure being rescued, which is the located evidence that tear production is the operative problem in the chronic stage (PMID 42663738, PMID 37026313). Recorded as documented association only, with the fact that the primary anchor is a management review that reports no rate, carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and NO LOCATED ANCHOR REPORTS A PREVALENCE OR SEVERITY DISTRIBUTION FOR CHRONIC OCULAR SURFACE DISEASE IN STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME SEPARATED FROM TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS, so this edge carries a management finding and no magnitude. The first anchor's population is titled as SJS AND TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS together and the review explicitly discusses the changing classification of the ocular disease, which is a strength for the management claim and a weakness for any prevalence claim. The primary anchor is a MANAGEMENT REVIEW, not a cohort, and it is registered for what it establishes rather than measures: that the chronic ocular problem requires a correct diagnosis of the underlying mechanism before treatment, that the rehabilitation pathway is built around restoring the tear film and the ocular surface, and that even the most aggressive surgical options have a LOW SUCCESS RATE in this population. The second and third anchors are likewise about therapy, and the third is a PILOT STUDY, so neither supplies a natural-history figure. A further caution is stated: ocular disease in this identity is commonly a MIXTURE of mechanisms, with the first anchor's own insistence on correctly identifying the underlying problem implying that epithelial loss, stem-cell deficiency, scarring, lid malposition and tear deficiency coexist in variable proportion, so an individual must not be assigned a single mechanism. Individual claims require a dated biopsy-supported or clinically definitive diagnosis with the severity grade, the body-site involvement percentage and the SJS, overlap or TEN classification documented, a dated ophthalmic assessment documenting acuity, ocular surface staining, tear-film breakup time, corneal sensation, limbal status and lid position, a documented ocular treatment history including any amniotic membrane or mucous membrane graft, and a clinical determination separating this identity's sequelae from a prior ocular surface disease, from graft-related complications and from unrelated dry eye.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesised vector is immune-mediated destruction of the ocular surface epithelium followed by a failure of the lacrimal unit to recover: the drug reaction targets the epithelium of the whole body, so the corneal and conjunctival epithelium is denuded at the same time as the skin, and the ocular surface then fails to re-epithelise normally because the limbal epithelial reservoir is depleted, the conjunctival epithelium is replaced by metaplastic squamous epithelium, and the lacrimal gland is itself inflamed and its ducts obstructed by the same process, so the recovered surface is a keratinised, insensate, poorly wetted surface over a deficient tear film, and it is that combination rather than any single lesion that produces the chronic syndrome; the vector is named as this epithelial and lacrimal unit failure because the located evidence treats the lacrimal gland and the ocular surface as one rehabilitation problem.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at management-review, therapeutic-systematic-review and therapeutic-pilot-study class, following the file's existing mucocutaneous, ophthalmic and autoimmune-reaction pathway scope. The management review is the anchor that carries the edge because it is the located source that establishes the chronic ocular problem as one of correct identification and of ocular surface rehabilitation, it names PUNCTAL OCCLUSION and scleral lens replacement of the ocular surface as the rehabilitative techniques, and it states that keratoplasty and keratoprosthesis success REMAINS LOW in this population, which is the located reason the edge is held at association only rather than escalated (PMID 41288622). The amniotic membrane systematic review is registered because it addresses the acute and chronic phases together, which is what makes it usable for a chronic-phase claim in an identity whose ocular disease is often assessed in the acute phase only (PMID 42663738). The pilot study is registered for a structural reason rather than a numerical one, namely that a targeted lacrimal gland therapy exists for this identity at all, which locates the failing structure, and its pilot status is disclosed so it supplies no rate (PMID 37026313). Because all three anchors are therapeutic in framing, all three merge this identity with toxic epidermal necrolysis, and none reports a natural-history prevalence, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only with no magnitude stated.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: NO LOCATED ANCHOR REPORTS A PREVALENCE OR SEVERITY DISTRIBUTION for chronic ocular surface disease in this identity SEPARATED FROM TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS, so this edge carries a MANAGEMENT FINDING AND NO MAGNITUDE (PMID 41288622, PMID 42663738, PMID 37026313). ALL THREE ANCHORS ARE THERAPEUTIC IN FRAMING, being a management review, a therapeutic systematic review and a therapeutic pilot study, and NONE IS A NATURAL-HISTORY COHORT, so none can state how many survivors develop chronic ocular disease or how severe it typically is (PMID 41288622, PMID 42663738, PMID 37026313). THE PRIMARY ANCHOR EXPLICITLY REPORTS THAT KERATOPLASTY AND KERATOPLASTESIS SUCCESS REMAINS LOW in this population, so the edge may not be used to imply that surgical correction reliably resolves the ocular sequelae (PMID 41288622). OCULAR DISEASE IN THIS IDENTITY IS COMMONLY A MIXTURE OF MECHANISMS, and the primary anchor's own insistence that it is OF THE UTMOST IMPORTANCE TO CORRECTLY IDENTIFY THE UNDERLYING PROBLEM in the chronic stage implies that epithelial loss, limbal stem-cell deficiency, scarring, lid malposition and tear deficiency coexist in variable proportion, so NO INDIVIDUAL MAY BE ASSIGNED A SINGLE MECHANISM (PMID 41288622). ALL THREE ANCHORS TITLE THEIR POPULATION AS STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME AND TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS TOGETHER, which the catalog carries as separate identities, so a finding in the more severe reaction may not be assumed to apply to this identity. THE THIRD ANCHOR IS A PILOT STUDY and supplies no rate. NO located anchor reports a natural-history time course, a proportion recovering without sequelae, an association with the acute-phase severity grade or the body-site involvement percentage, or any effect of early ophthalmic intervention on the chronic outcome.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Toxic epidermal necrolysis, which the catalog carries as a separate identity, is merged into every located anchor and is a more severe reaction with its own ocular burden, so a TEN finding may not be transferred to this identity
A pre-existing ocular surface disease such as dry eye, keratoconjunctivitis sicca, a prior ocular graft or prior ocular surgery, which would produce ocular symptoms by an independent route

Graft-related complications including recurrent graft failure, epithelial rejection and infection of a keratoplasty or keratoprosthesis, which the primary anchor's low-success-rate statement makes a live confounder in any treated eye
Direct ocular toxicity of a medication rather than the hypersensitivity reaction itself, which can produce a dry eye that is reversible on withdrawal and is not a sequela of this identity

Exposure keratopathy from incomplete eyelid closure or ocular surface exposure following facial scarring, which is a mechanical sequel rather than an inflammatory one and is not separated in any located anchor

suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers this edge because chronic ocular surface disease is the most durable physical sequela of this identity and the located evidence documents the rehabilitation problem it creates, and because the target identity, dry-eye-syndrome, is thinly covered in the registry while this catalog identity had ZERO registered edges. The conservative framing is explicit that all three anchors are therapeutic rather than natural-history, that all three merge this identity with toxic epidermal necrolysis, and that the primary anchor reports low success rates for the definitive surgical options.

sourceReferences.citation: Akgun Z, Can GD, Selver OB. Ocular involvement in Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis: A review of current management and changing trends. Indian J Ophthalmol. 2025 Dec 1;73(12):1711-1722. doi: 10.4103/IJO.IJO_1119_25. PMID 41288622.
sourceReferences.note: REVIEW OF OCULAR INVOLVEMENT IN STEVENS-JOHNSON SYNDROME AND TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS covering the evolution of acute and chronic stage classification and the corresponding changes in management. AMNIOTIC MEMBRANE TRANSPLANTATION is described as efficacious for controlling acute inflammation particularly in severe or extreme presentations, with practical methods such as sutureless placement introduced. The authors state that TO MANAGE THE CHRONIC STAGE IT IS OF THE UTMOST IMPORTANCE TO CORRECTLY IDENTIFY THE UNDERLYING PROBLEM, and that beyond minor salivary gland transplantation and PUNCTAL OCCLUSION the REHABILITATIVE MANAGEMENT OF THE OCULAR SURFACE encompasses specially designed scleral lenses, specifically Prosthetic Replacement of the Ocular Surface Ecosystem; autologous mucosal membrane grafting has recently seen a resurgence, and cultured and simple limbal epithelial transplantation represent significant advances. CRITICALLY, THE SUCCESS RATE OF KERATOPLASTY AND KERATOPLASTESIS REMAINS LOW, although establishing good ocular surface homeostasis beforehand significantly improves the outcome. Registered as the anchor that establishes the chronic ocular problem as one of correct identification and ocular surface rehabilitation, and as the located source for the low-success-rate caveat. DISCLOSED: a MANAGEMENT REVIEW reporting no prevalence, with the population titled as SJS AND TOXIC EPIDERMAL NECROLYSIS together.

governanceNotes: IDENTITY SCREEN, batch 87: NO ALIAS DUPLICATION, but a SPECTRUM FINDING of the same kind as batch 86's spermatocele finding and recorded as such. toxic-epidermal-necrolysis and cicatricial-pemphigoid and bullous-pemphigoid are separate catalog identities. The literature located for this file merges Stevens-Johnson syndrome with toxic epidermal necrolysis in every case, including in the titles of the systematic review, the multicentre survey and the paediatric cohort, so the catalog is FINER-grained than the evidence on a spectrum that is clinically continuous. No edge is registered to toxic-epidermal-necrolysis and the guard is declared in the todo list so it is durable.

INCOMING-EDGE MAP, batch 87: this identity had ZERO registered incoming edges and ZERO registered outgoing edges before this batch, so all three edges are new. Targets depressive-disorder at 94 and anxiety-disorder at 27 are among the most heavily targeted identities in the registry, and dry-eye-syndrome is thinly covered.

SHARED-ANCHOR-SET DISCLOSURE: the depressive-disorder and anxiety-disorder edges share two of three anchors, and the third anchor on the anxiety edge is class-level rather than identity-specific. The two mood edges are therefore NOT independent lines of evidence, and the anxiety edge is ranked second partly for that reason.

A LATE-EMERGING-SEQUELAE FINDING CARRIED ACROSS THE FILE: the paediatric follow-up cohort reports that two patients whose eye examination was NORMAL IN THE ACUTE PHASE had ocular involvement in the chronic period, and that antinuclear antibody values were positive at follow-up having been negative at first admission in three patients. This is recorded in the file todo list because it is the located reason a chronic-phase assessment is required before any sequela may be claimed, and it applies to the mood and ocular edges alike.

ANCHOR-TIER DECLARATION: the ocular edge's three anchors are a management review, a therapeutic systematic review and a therapeutic pilot study, and NONE is a natural-history cohort. That is stated on the face of the edge and in the governance notes rather than presented as a weakness discovered later.
